text:
Maya (Sales): Quick sync. Large fintech prospect asking for a 12mo commit. They expect long tail bursts: baseline ~800 RPS, periodic spikes to 6k RPS for ~8-12 minutes. Need recommended reserved GPU footprint + autoscale pattern and a blunt cost comparison for reserved 12 vs reserved 18.
Diego (AE): They want predictable p95 <120ms for single-turn chats (avg ~50 tokens). Also insist on EU-only data residency. Could be Dedicated.
Priya (SolutionsEng): Clarifying: are these user sessions with KV cache? Any expectation for cold-warm mix?
Maya (Sales): Customer estimates 65% KV cache hit for repeat users; 15% of requests include long contexts (~300 tokens), rest are short.
Noah (SRE): Ballpark: with quantized Llama, per-GPU peak RPS (short requests) ~200. For mixed long-context traffic effective RPS drops. For steady 800 -> ~4-5 GPUs. For 6k bursts -> ~30 GPUs.
Hannah (Infra): Recommend split strategy: reserve to cover 24-48h steady + buffer for small ramps, use burst credits/autoscale to reach peak. Two configurations to compare:
A) Reserve 12 GPUs + aggressive burst to 36
B) Reserve 18 GPUs + smaller burst to 30
Priya (SolutionsEng): Perf vs cost tradeoff: A costs less reserved, but risk of queueing for sudden spikes; B costs more committed but smoother p95. Also consider model-variant fallback: when saturated, route to smaller model with ~2x throughput to keep latency.
Maya (Sales): They asked for a simple policy example and preheat options tied to business schedule.
Priya (SolutionsEng): Example autoscale snippet (JSON):
```json
{"min_gpus":"12","max_gpus":"36","scale_up":{"type":"rps","window_s":45,"threshold_rps_per_gpu":170},"preheat_schedules":[{"cron":"0 7 * * 1-5","tz":"Europe/Berlin","preheat_seconds":600}],"fallback":"small-quantized-variant"}
```
Noah (SRE): Operational notes: preheat should be two-stage: 1) KV warm (fast, seconds) 2) model weight warm (longer, tens of seconds). Use rolling preheat across AZs to avoid thundering herd. Also set queue caps so requests get early fallback rather than piling up.
Hannah (Infra): For EU residency, Dedicated clusters in eu-west can attach customer KMS. That changes the pricing band; include both hosted vs dedicated estimates.
Maya (Sales): Cost table request: monthly committed cost + expected variable usage for burst minutes. Can we give a delta % between Reserve12 vs Reserve18 for hosted and for dedicated?
Priya (SolutionsEng): I'll run perf sims tonight with 65% KV hit and mixed context. Will output p95 and effective token/sec per GPU.
Noah (SRE): I'll estimate expected queueing delay under both configs and recommend per-GPU queue-depth settings. Also include recommended cooldowns for scale-down to avoid oscillation (suggest 4-6m).
Maya (Sales): Great. Who owns the slide with scenario numbers?
Priya (SolutionsEng): I will. Noah -> ops notes + queue guidance. Hannah -> pricing buckets (hosted vs dedicated + KMS addon). Maya/Diego -> confirm customer cadence and ask them about predictable peak windows for preheat.
deploy-bot: capacity-sim job started (id: cap-sim-1799).
Noah (SRE): Sim quicklook: with 65% KV hit, Reserve12+burst to36 -> p95 ~125ms, Reserve18+burst to30 -> p95 ~110ms during 6k spike. Cost delta (hosted) approx +1.5x for Reserve18 vs Reserve12 on committed charges; dedicated multipliers to be provided by Hannah.
Maya (Sales): Perfect. Customer meeting Fri AM. Can we have a one-pager and the two-number table by Thu EOD?
Priya (SolutionsEng): Yes, will deliver.
Hannah (Infra): I'll prioritize pricing numbers and a short note on KMS workflow.
Maya (Sales): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Diego (AE): Adding a note: include a short "worst-case graceful degradation" blurb for the legal/security team.
Priya (SolutionsEng): Will include.
